title: From Maps to Metabolism: Historical Precedents and a Unified Critique of Computationalism
abstract: arXiv:2611.06936v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Alexander Lerchner's recent work on the 'abstraction fallacy' argues that computational functionalism confuses physical processes with abstract descriptions, and that symbolic computation alone cannot instantiate consciousness. Yet these claims were anticipated by Korzybski's map-territory distinction, Searle's critique of strong artificial intelligence, Floridi's levels of abstraction, Spencer et al.'s observer-relativity arguments, Winograd and Flores's account of computation as socially grounded practice, and Nasuto and Bishop's biological arguments. Synthesizing these contributions, this paper advances a form of non-computational physicalism: consciousness depends upon intrinsically organized, metabolically grounded physical dynamics rather than abstract computation, whilst leaving open the possibility of artificial consciousness.   An objection is that this critique targets an outdated computationalism. Mechanistic computationalis

translated_title: 从地图到新陈代谢：历史先例与对计算主义的统一批判
translated_abstract: 亚历山大·莱希纳近期关于“抽象谬误”的研究认为，计算功能主义混淆了物理过程与抽象描述，且单纯的符号计算无法实现意识。然而这些主张早已被科日布斯基的“地图-疆域”之别、塞尔对强人工智能的批判、弗洛里迪的抽象层级理论、斯宾塞等人的观察者相对性论证、温诺格拉德与弗洛雷斯关于计算作为社会性根植实践的阐释，以及纳苏托和毕晓普的生物学论证所预见。通过综合这些贡献，本文提出了一种非计算物理主义：意识依赖于内在组织的、以新陈代谢为基础的物理动力学，而非抽象计算，同时不排除人工意识存在的可能性。有一种反对意见认为，这一批判针对的只是过时的计算主义。机械论计算主义……
tldr: 本文综合科日布斯基、塞尔、弗洛里迪等多位学者的历史先例，提出一种非计算物理主义，主张意识依赖于以新陈代谢为基础的物理动力学而非抽象计算，但并不排除人工意识的可能性。
en_tdlr: This paper synthesizes historical precedents from Korzybski, Searle, Floridi, and others to advance a form of non-computational physicalism, arguing that consciousness depends on metabolically grounded physical dynamics rather than abstract computation, while leaving open the possibility of artificial consciousness.
